rows.quote: Fenland, a proteome-wide proteome association study of 10,708 participants of European ancestry, used the SomaScan v4 assay with 4979 single-stranded oligonucleotides (aptamers) targeting 4775 unique proteins [13].
rows.reference_quote: Pietzner M, Wheeler E, Carrasco-Zanini J, Cortes A, Koprulu M, Wörheide MA et al. Mapping the proteo-genomic convergence of human diseases. Sci (New York NY).374(6569):eabj1541.
rows.coder_note: Step 2 of the decision order (uniquely identifying citation): the sentence attributes the Fenland dataset to reference 13, whose DOI 10.1126/science.abj1541 is the source identifier of exactly one pqtl row; 10,708 and SomaScan v4 are shared by both Fenland rows and do not separate them, and the sentence's 4979 aptamers and 4775 proteins are those of the Pietzner 2021 row. No conflict in the other passages. No accession for this row (ukb-d-C_LYMPHOMA is the outcome dataset's).

rows.quote: Using the SomaScan Multiple Aptamer Assay (version 4) in 35,559 Icelandic individuals with genotypic and phenotypic data, the deCODE study measured plasma protein levels [12], including 4,907 aptamers and 4,719 proteins.
rows.coder_note: Step 2 of the decision order (exact N with platform): 35,559 Icelandic individuals on SomaScan version 4 with 4,907 aptamers matches exactly one pqtl row (the other deCODE row has 35,892); reference 12 in the same sentence (Ferkingstad 2021, doi:10.1038/s41588-021-00978-w) agrees. No conflict in the other passages. No accession for this row.
